text: Fill in the blanks with the correct drug name, mechanism, or duration from the WHO MDT regimen for leprosy.
questions: Paucibacillary leprosy (1–5 lesions, BI negative) is treated for *6/six:PB = shorter duration* months with rifampicin and dapsone.
Multibacillary leprosy adds *Clofazimine/clofazimine:This drug also has anti-inflammatory properties and causes skin discolouration* to the rifampicin-dapsone backbone for 12 months.
Rifampicin inhibits *RNA polymerase/RNA Polymerase/DNA-dependent RNA polymerase:Same target as in TB treatment* and is the most potent bactericidal drug in the MDT regimen.
Dapsone inhibits *dihydropteroate synthase/DHPS:Same enzyme targeted by sulphonamides*, acting as a bacteriostatic folate antagonist.
The supervised monthly pulse dose of rifampicin in both PB and MB regimens is *600:Given once monthly under direct observation* mg.
